title: Introduce opaque Retry-Advice header and idempotency-session for streamed API calls
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes:
- Add opaque Retry-Advice header for machine-readable backoff guidance
- Introduce idempotency-session token for streamed tool/function calls to disambiguate retries
- Clarify Retry-After precedence (explicit header > Retry-Advice TTL > heuristic)
- Compatibility shim for OpenAI-style clients: best-effort mapping to existing Retry-After semantics
description:
Background and motivation: We observed multiple production incidents where streaming tool calls retried incorrectly due to ambiguous Retry-After semantics and lack of a per-session idempotency context. OpenAI-compatible clients expect simple Retry-After behavior, but multiplexed streams and function/tool calls need richer signals so that SDKs and proxies can make correct retrying decisions without accidental double-execution. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a machine-readable, opaque Retry-Advice header (X-Redwood-Retry-Advice) that encodes backoff windows and optional short-term lease tokens for idempotency coordination; and (2) an Idempotency-Session token surfaced in stream init frames and the HTTP layer to tie retries to a single logical session across reconnects.

Summary of changes:
- API layer: add X-Redwood-Retry-Advice header generator and parser, documented encoding (base64 JSON envelope) and fallback rules.
- Stream protocol: include idempotency_session_id in the initial handshake frame (and as an HTTP header for non-streamed endpoints).
- SDK compat: OpenAI-compat adapter maps Retry-Advice to Retry-After when possible and logs advisory reasons.
- Server runtime: produce Retry-Advice on capacity-related 429s and transient worker errors; conservative advice when admission control is uncertain.
- Tests: unit tests for header encoding/decoding, integration tests with reconnect+retry scenarios, and a small load test demonstrating reduced duplicate tool invocations.
- Docs: API surface doc updates and migration guidance for SDKs and proxies.

Compatibility and semantics:
- The Retry-Advice header is opaque to clients: it encodes a JSON envelope with fields (advice_ttl_seconds, recommended_backoff_ms, lease_token_optional, reason). The header is base64(json) and intended for SDKs and proxies that can parse it.
- Fallback precedence: 1) If Retry-After header is present and the server explicitly set it, clients SHOULD honor it. 2) If X-Redwood-Retry-Advice is present, clients MAY use its recommended_backoff_ms as an advisory. 3) If neither is present, clients follow existing exponential backoff heuristics.
- Idempotency-session: when present, it is a server-side ephemeral opaque token (UUIDv4-like) that ties the logical tool/function invocation session across reconnects; clients include it on reconnect attempts so the server can associate retries with prior state and avoid duplicate function invocations.

Observability and rollout:
- New metrics: retry_advice_emitted{reason}, idempotency_session_reused, duplicate_tool_invocations_blocked
- Create dashboards for retriable-errors, percent of streaming reconnects using idempotency_session
- Rollout plan: staged on Canary (10%), then Dedicated, then Hosted. Feature flag gated for first 2 weeks.

Migration guidance for SDKs:
- Parse X-Redwood-Retry-Advice when available and prefer its numeric fields for backoff decisions.
- On reconnect, include previous idempotency_session_id if network error occurred within TTL.
- OpenAI-compat adapter continues to expose Retry-After for simplicity but logs the presence of Retry-Advice for future migration.

Tests and CI:
- Unit tests added for encoder/decoder and handshake behavior
- Integration test simulates reconnect with a tool call: server returns retry-advice and subsequent reconnect includes idempotency_session -> server suppresses duplicate invocation
- Load test with 1000 concurrent short streams shows duplicate tool invocations drop by ~72% vs. baseline with naive retries.
- CI initially failed on lint (openapi spec mismatch), fixed in follow-up commit and all checks passed.

Review thread (highlights):
"Jonas Rivera (reviewer): The envelope looks fine but we should avoid leaking actionable tokens to user logs — ensure lease_token is redacted in telemetry." — Author reply: "Agreed; lease_token is marked sensitive and only hashed before emitting to logs; updated telemetry code in b5d2e10." "Priya Shah (reviewer): How does this interact with long-tail client libraries that only look at Retry-After?" — Author reply: "OpenAI-compat maps the numeric recommended_backoff_ms to Retry-After seconds when present; docs added to guide SDKs on gradual migration (see docs/guides/retry_advice.md)." "Samir Kulkarni: Can we avoid adding a new header if Retry-After already suffices?" — Author reply: "We emit Retry-Advice only when richer context is available (e.g., lease_token or precise backoff_window) or when we anticipate reconnection attempts; otherwise we keep current Retry-After behavior." "QA: Found a race in session reuse on reconnect when two reconnects happen concurrently; fixed by session compare-and-set in stream manager (commit e4c1027)." "OPS: Please add metric for 'retry_advice_issued' tagged by region — added telemetry change and dashboard sample."

CI timeline:
- Initial run (2026-01-20): unit tests pass, integration tests flaky (2/4), lint failed (openapi docs)
- Fixes applied (2026-01-24): bump openapi schema and stabilize integration, re-run CI
- Final run (2026-01-29): all checks green (unit+integration+lint+e2e), canary load test executed in staging with expected reduction in duplicate tool calls.

Merge rationale and outcome: This change improves robustness of streamed tool/function calls by giving richer, machine-readable guidance for backoff and a mechanism to reliably identify retry sessions. It is backwards compatible with clients that only observe Retry-After. After approvals from reviewers and successful staging canary, the branch was squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-02.

Notes and future work:
- Proposal to standardize Retry-Advice envelope across other Redwood services (follow-up ENG-8699).
- Consider exposing a lightweight, non-sensitive 'retry_hint' JSON in a future minor release for non-SDK proxies.
- SDK changes (python/ts/go) will land in separate PRs that consume the header and implement session reuse logic.
